chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, both together from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who speaks forgetfully during the salat (prayer), saying, “Straighten your rows.” He said: “He completes his salat (prayer), then performs two sajdahs.” I said: “Are the two sajdahs of forgetfulness before the taslīm or after it?” He said: “After it.”

key_terms.التَّسْلِيمِ: the concluding salutation that ends the prayer
key_terms.سَجْدَتَا السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations of forgetfulness performed to remedy an inadvertent mistake in prayer
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيْنِ: two sajdahs; the two prostrations required here
key_terms.صُفُوفَكُمْ: your rows; referring to the prayer rows of the congregation
key_terms.نَاسِيًا: forgetfully; speaking unintentionally due to forgetfulness
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: he completes; meaning the prayer is to be finished rather than broken

ai.seo_question: If someone speaks forgetfully during salat (prayer), should they perform sajdatay al-sahw before or after the taslīm?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who speaks forgetfully during salat (prayer). The Imam عليه السلام states that the prayer is completed and then two sajdahs of forgetfulness are performed after the taslīm.
